blanks.note: No gold to custody. Reserve Bank of New Zealand's own Official Information Act response of 24 August 2023 to FYI requests 23611/23613 (published at fyi.org.nz, 'Official information request relating to legal tender, gold reserve sales, and sovereign debt', p.2, answer to the gold-sales question) states: 'The below chart shows RBNZ gold holdings by year. You will note that approximately $14m of gold was sold around 1989/1990. Gold holdings would have been classified as foreign reserves at the time.' The accompanying chart is an image and extracts as nothing, but the text is unambiguous that the holding was sold out around 1989/1990, and the answer treats gold as a past holding throughout. There is therefore no custodian to find; any future round should treat NZL as a structural blank rather than an unread document. Source URL: https://fyi.org.nz/request/23611/response/89405/attach/5/OIA2324%20007%20008%20Response.pdf

Banco de Espana, Cuentas Anuales 2023 (repositorio.bde.es/bitstream/123456789/36256/1/BE_CuentasAnuales_2023.pdf), note 'Oro y derechos en oro' read: gives only 'Las tenencias de oro al cierre del ejercicio se elevan a 16.910,85 millones de euros, equivalentes a 9,054 millones de onzas troy de oro fino' and names no depositary, no institution and no city (no Banco de Inglaterra, no Reserva Federal, no BPI). The FX-reserves-structure lever was tried and also fails: Informe Institucional 2024, Capitulo 5 'Informacion financiera' (bde.es/f/webbe/INF/MenuHorizontal/Publicaciones/PublicacionesAnuales/InformeInstitucional/2024/INI2024_Capitulo5.pdf, 38,928 characters of text read in full) itemises the foreign-currency portfolio by currency and by instrument type (graphic 5.4) and the gold holding separately (p. text lines 530-534, graphic 5.5: 9,054 million fine troy ounces constant 2020-2024, market value EUR 22,735 million at end-2024) without naming any holder or location for the metal. Not yet read: the second half (characters 100,000-181,678) of the Cuentas Anuales 2023 PDF, which is income statement and post-reserves notes, and the Cuentas Anuales 2024 edition. Repositorio.bde.es returns HTTP 403 to curl; WebFetch serves it.

Bank of Greece publishes its annual financial statements only as the ATHEX filing 'Financial Statement - Full Notes BANK OF GREECE S.A.'. Both the 2024 edition (athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes/2025-03/2791eee6-6324-4b5b-98e3-804b83dfb338/Financial%20Statement%20-%20Full%20Notes%20BANK%20OF%20GREECE%20S.A.%20%282024%2CYear%20Statement%2CCompany%29.pdf) and the 2025 edition (athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/en/3ad3f0aa-ebae-4b0d-93f0-aaebae9b0d97/Financial%20statement%20BANK%20OF%20GREECE%20S.A.%20%282025%2CAnnual%20report%2CParent%29.pdf) were downloaded and read in full (25,181 and 25,167 characters of extracted text respectively). The balance-sheet line 'Gold and gold receivables' is explained only by note 2 to the statements: 'Gold has been valued at the price provided by the ECB as at 31.12.2025: EUR 3,669.106 per fine ounce, compared with EUR 2,511.069 as at 31.12.2024' - valuation only, no tonnage split, no depositary, no city. The only occurrence of the word custody in either document is in the description of the Bank's own services, 'and custody of assets of public entities, social security funds and private agents', which is the Bank acting as custodian for third parties and not a statement about its own gold. No FX-reserves structure or composition section exists in this abridged filing, so that lever cannot be applied; a fuller Greek-language annex to the Governor's Annual Report was searched for twice and did not surface.

Central Bank of Sri Lanka, 'Financial Statements and Operations 2024' (cbsl.gov.lk/sites/default/files/cbslweb_documents/publications/fsor/2024/en/financial-statements-operations.pdf, 548,403 characters of extracted text, grepped in full). Note 18 'Gold' gives only the statutory basis and the quantity: 'Section 40 (2) of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka Act ... states that gold including credit balances representing such gold may be held by the CBSL as part of the international reserves. This includes Gold weighted 15,148.163 Bar Fine Ounce as at 31 December 2024 (2023 - 15,148.163 Bar Fine Ounce) priced at USD 2,624.01 per troy ounce'. Accounting policy 7.14 'Gold' repeats the same statutory wording and adds only fair-value treatment. Three further levers were tried and all fail: (a) the reserve-management narrative in the same volume ('Investment instruments and portfolio management') says the investment portfolio includes 'gold investments, securities lending (managed by custodians on behalf of CBSL)' but names no custodian and does not tie one to gold; (b) the credit-risk counterparty table lists Federal Reserve Bank - USA / Reserve Bank of Australia / Bank for International Settlements / Bank of Japan / Deutsche Bundesbank / Bank of England / Sveriges Riksbank / Bank of Canada / Reserve Bank of New Zealand / Reserve Bank of India / People's Bank of China - but that list sits against the row 'Cash and Cash Equivalents', not against gold, which is exactly the trap the brief warns of, so it names no gold custodian; (c) note 52.1.8 'The Bank also has custodial arrangements with one State-controlled bank, for which no charges were levied' names no bank and is a related-party disclosure about the CBSL providing custody, not receiving it. The only named global custodian in the document, Euroclear (note at line 30037), is tied to AUD collateral for auto bond lending, not gold.

Nepal Rastra Bank, Financial Statement FY 2077/78 (2020/21) (nrb.org.np/contents/uploads/2021/11/Financial-Statement-2077_78-1.pdf, 180,899 characters, grepped in full). Note 4.4 'Gold & Silver at Fair Value' and the explanatory note 5.1 'Gold and Silver' split the holding into 'Investment in Paper Gold' (5,863.058408 kg, NRs 44,655,278,083) and 'Gold held in Stock' (1,953.662100 kg, NRs 15,610,737,010), plus silver. Neither names a vault, an institution or a city. Note 5.1 says only 'For gold physically held with the bank, the rate for Fine Gold (9999) has been considered for the purpose of fair value' - the bank as holder but with no place named, which this row's place-must-be-named rule refuses. The paper-gold leg is a gold deposit earning interest (income statement line 'Interest Income from Foreign Gold Deposit', and the weighted-average-interest schedule lists 'Investment in Paper Gold' beside US Government Treasury Notes and time deposits), which the row's rules exclude as not saying where metal sits, and no counterparty is named for it anywhere. Accounting policy 3.16 'Gold and Silver at fair value' and 3.17 'Inventories' add nothing on location. Not read: the FY 2079/80 (2022/23) financial statement at nrb.org.np/fmd/financial-statement-fy-2022-23-2079-80, which appears to use the same template.

Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) publishes no notes to its financial statements. Its Balance Sheet 2025 (cbc.gov.tw/en/dl-227340-3902a8b8eacc4688acf54d967ae3e340.html, one page) carries gold only inside an aggregate, with the single explanatory note: 'Foreign Assets include gold, deposits with foreign banks, and securities issued by foreign governments' - no gold line of its own, no holder, no place. The CBC Annual Report 2025, chapter 3 'Foreign Exchange Management' (cbc.gov.tw/dl-225846-905d3e594a524e47987afb5abb5bf0ee.html, 7 pages, read in full) states 'Combining the reserves held in gold valued at US$4.9 billion, the Bank's reserve assets totaled US$607.5 billion at the end of the year' and sets out the reserve portfolio by currency against the IMF COFER average, naming no custodian and no location for the metal. The only use of the word custodian in the chapter is a rule change allowing offshore securities branches 'to deposit offshore customer funds with foreign custodian banks', which is about banks' customer funds and not the CBC's gold. Vein note: the CBC has long declined to confirm storage locations publicly, so the remaining route would be Legislative Yuan committee records rather than the bank's own publications.

Next document to open: the BCTL Annual Report listing page at bancocentral.tl/publication/bctl_ann_rep/, to recover a working direct link to the most recent Annual Report and its audited financial statements, then grep the statements for gold. Worth knowing before spending much: Timor-Leste is dollarised and the BCTL's reserve assets are dominated by the Petroleum Fund, so a nil gold holding is the likely answer and would itself be a close.
